headline: Ross holiday-quarter comps rose 9%, far above its 3-4% plan, with customer counts growing; FY26 guide initiated.
guidance_note: FY26 guide: comp +3-4%, EPS $7.02-7.36 (vs ~$7.22 consensus). Q1 comp +7-8%, EPS $1.60-1.67.
key_messages: Comp +9% vs 3-4% plan and ~5.1% analyst view; operating margin 12.3% vs 11.5-11.8% plan.
Conroy: 'nice customer count growth,' notably among 18-34 year olds, helped by more brands in assortments.
Home was the business 'most under attack with tariffs' early in 2025 but recovered; FY25 tariff cost ~$0.16/share.
FY25 sales a record $22.8bn; new two-year $2.55bn buyback authorized.

consumer.big_ticket: Home business recovered after early-2025 tariff disruption.
consumer.pricing: Tariff-related costs ~$0.16/share for FY25; home most affected.
consumer.quote: We're very encouraged that we are seeing nice customer count growth

macro_read: Traffic-led holiday strength at Ross, especially among younger shoppers, shows value retail gaining share despite tariff costs.

sources.label: Dow Jones: Ross 4Q sales rise as traffic picks up
